obsidian-plum.$description: Obsidian Plum — Page canvas, deepest background — the negative space headlines float on

graphite-plum.$description: Graphite Plum — Card and list surface — one step lifted from the canvas, carries testimonial cards and feature lists

smoke-plum.$description: Smoke Plum — Inner card surface and hairline border on cards — a second elevation step

ink-border.$description: Ink Border — Subtle violet-tinted borders and dividers between elements

carbon.$description: Carbon — Navigation fills and tonal mid-ground blocks

mist-gray.$description: Mist Gray — Body text, nav links, secondary icons — the dominant cool-gray voice for readable but non-emphatic text

soft-mist.$description: Soft Mist — Lighter body text variant for de-emphasized content

bone.$description: Bone — Hairline borders across the entire system — the connective tissue between every section, card, and list

paper.$description: Paper — Light text on dark surfaces, inverse labels, and high-contrast captions. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

signal-mint.$description: Signal Mint — Green text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases

mint-halo.$description: Mint Halo — Soft mint highlight wash, inset glow on hero elements, gradient terminator fading to white

electric-violet.$description: Electric Violet — Feature pill icons, secondary accents, gradient terminator — the cool counterpart to mint, carries the decorative gradient text

deep-violet.$description: Deep Violet — Decorative card fill, gradient start — a deeper violet used sparingly for tonal richness

lilac.$description: Lilac — Light accent text and headings — soft violet for non-body highlights

mauve.$description: Mauve — Muted violet for body text accents and secondary icon strokes

jam-pink.$description: Jam Pink — Red wash for highlight backgrounds, decorative bands, and soft emphasis behind content. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

oldschool-grotesk.$description: Display and heading face — the signature font. Weight 900 at 66–116px for hero headlines, weight 400 for small caps and labels. This custom geometric grotesk gives Jam its voice: the 900-weight is not just bold, it is architectural, and the compressed letterforms make even short words feel like monuments. At 8–16px it functions as an uppercase micro-label for trust badges and nav accents.

sf-pro-text.$description: UI body and interface text — the workhorse. Sizes 14–16px at weight 400–500 for body and nav, 600–700 for button labels. The -0.025em letter-spacing tightens the default SF Pro into a denser, more deliberate reading rhythm that matches the display font's compressed character.

sf-mono.$description: Monospaced code fragments and technical micro-labels — sparingly used for inline technical annotations
